📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #112 in the last 7 days.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@crm experience` / `#team-crm-experience`)
Playbook: Confirm shape (monitor ID among the 5 team:crm AMQP-consumer siblings) → pull `dd_search.py metric` for the fired service over a multi-hour window (expect a genuine but brief dip below floor, not a data gap) → confirm `service:<name> status:error` = 0 in DD Logs → check sibling latency/5xx monitor is also OK → if unresolved after ~1h or a sibling co-fires, escalate. Do not re-investigate from scratch each recurrence.
Open Jira: n/a — none filed

  • DD logs: service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber status:error, 06:04:21–07:24:21Z = 0 hits

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #30 in the last 7 days.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@crm experience` / `#team-crm-experience`)
Playbook: Re-query `p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod}` over the monitor's own literal pre-fire eval window (not just the single alerting bucket — DD's metric API has a documented resampling/rollup artifact for this monitor: a single huge point at a coarse interval that vanishes at the monitor's real evaluation granularity). Confirm `service:notifications status:error` = 0. If the literal eval window shows a genuine sustained breach instead of a rollup artifact, escalate — that would be the first real occurrence.
Open Jira: n/a — none filed

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 8)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)

Symptoms:
  - `ms-tables-fields-api` (DD tag `service:tables-fields`) p95 request latency spiked to 47.49s in a single 10s bucket at 08:06:30Z, ~12 min before monitor 299251779 tripped at 08:18:39Z (consistent with this monitor's documented rolling-window evaluation lag — the real excursion sits before the eval window, not inside it)
  - Monitor self-recovered to OK by scan time; only 1 Error-level log line in the ±10-min window around the spike ("Failed to SaveViewBundleInternal"), no sustained error burst
  - This is the **5th refutation** of `ki-2026-07-06-tables-fields-redis-circuitbreaker-p95-latency` against this monitor: neither the Redis-circuit-breaker evidence_query nor the app-update-agent "App Publish - Started" disqualifier returned any hits in the pre-spike window (both 0/6538 baseline log volume — normal traffic)

Trace IDs: n/a — no APM trace sample captured this cycle (single-bucket metric spike, not corroborated in DD Logs/APM trace search)
Likely cause: Unexplained, brief (single 10s bucket) tables-fields p95 latency excursion. Neither of the two previously-confirmed mechanisms for this monitor (Redis connectivity blip, app-update-push load storm) reproduced. Same "no identifiable mechanism" shape as the 2026-07-30 refutations (2 that day) — Ben previously flagged this KB entry for tightening/splitting by mechanism; this occurrence adds further weight to that recommendation.
Suggested next action: monitor — no actionable single-account or infra signal to act on this cycle; if this shape recurs again, consider Ben's standing recommendation to split `ki-2026-07-06-tables-fields-redis-circuitbreaker-p95-latency` into a confirmed-Redis-mechanism entry and a separate "tables-fields p95, no identifiable mechanism" entry so future cycles don't re-run the same disqualifier checks from scratch.

  • DD logs (disqualifier checks): `fields.dd_service.keyword:"tables-fields" AND message.keyword:"Redis Cache Circuit Breaker OPENED for 30 seconds due to: Recent Redis error detected"` = 0 hits; `fields.dd_service.keyword:"app-update-agent" AND message:"App Publish - Started"` = 0 hits

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-29-methodsession-getaccountbysubdomain-nre`
This is occurrence #30 in the last 7 days.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Playbook: Confirm synthetic-only via ES aggregate on message:'JWT Retrieval Failed' by UserAgent (100% WindowsPowerShell = no customer impact). Two independent fixes: (a) CODE — null guard in Com.Method.ServiceContract MethodSessionService.GetAccountBySubdomain() (TFS-built, not in GitHub clones — route to platform-ui/MethodUI backend owner); (b) MONITORING — fix the Centreon synthetic check to send a valid subdomain/Host header. Until fixed, #alert-system will keep getting intermittent fires — treat as monitoring noise, not a customer outage.
Open Jira: n/a — none filed

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 9)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: env  •  alerts in group: 2
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)   ← inert text per Hard rule #13

Symptoms:
  - DD monitor 299251779 "tables-fields 95th percentile latency" fired 15:50:40Z (threshold 1s), and monitor 302103451 "tables-fields p95 request latency" fired 15:54:31Z (threshold 0.25s) — same underlying metric, both self-recovered
  - p95 spiked to 5.254s peak at 15:46:20Z, an 80s excursion (8 buckets over 1s threshold)
  - App-Update-Agent "Push Update" job (Home Watch Admin v206) started 15:46:13Z, 7s before the spike onset — first cycle this disqualifier check found a positive correlated event instead of 0 hits
  - Redis-circuit-breaker mechanism (ki-2026-07-06's declared evidence_query) returned 0 hits — refutes that KB's specific mechanism, 6th refutation on record

Trace IDs: n/a — pure APM percentile signal, no representative trace pulled
Likely cause: transient collateral load on ms-tables-fields-api triggered by an App-Update-Agent Push Update job (Home Watch Admin v206), not the Redis-circuit-breaker mechanism of ki-2026-07-06. Timing-correlated (7s gap), not confirmed via direct trace linkage — confidence 0.65.
Suggested next action: monitor; if this app-update-push correlation repeats, consider filing a defect to add backpressure/rate-limiting between App-Update-Agent bulk field-metadata writes and tables-fields, or splitting ki-2026-07-06 into a Redis-confirmed variant and a load-driven variant
